_source: GFMAM Asset Management Landscape v3.0 (third edition, June 2024)
_notice: GFMAM Asset Management Landscape, third edition, June 2024, ISBN 978-1-7774676-8-5, Global Forum on Maintenance and Asset Management. Subject numbers and names are cited for identification. Definitions are quoted only where read verbatim from the published PDF and are attributed inline.
_why: GFMAM is an asset management AUTHORITY. APQC is a benchmarking taxonomy. A gap that both show is corroborated by two independent organisations, which is this repository's promotion threshold.

rows.name: Organisational Purpose and Context
rows.note: Management-system subject.

rows.name: Stakeholder Management
rows.note: Customer communication and pipeline public awareness only. No stakeholder management as a discipline, which is correct for a process reference.

rows.name: Asset Costing and Valuation
rows.note: The model settles cost to the work order and unitises it to the property record. It does not value the asset base.

rows.name: Asset Management Policy
rows.note: Management-system subject.

rows.name: Asset Management System
rows.note: Management-system subject.

rows.name: Asset Management Assurance and Audit
rows.note: Audit exists per programme - vegetation, DIMP, reporting obligations - but there is no assurance process over the asset management system itself.

rows.name: Technical Standards & Legislation
rows.note: Regulatory obligation register plus the compliance category.

rows.name: Management of Change
rows.note: Change to authorised work scope (2.3.5) and asset-related technical change (12.6.4). No organisational or management-system change process, which is correct here.

rows.name: Risk
rows.note: Asset risk and consequence of failure, and the distribution integrity programme.

rows.name: Asset Management Strategy and Objectives
rows.note: Strategy setting sits above a work management reference.

rows.name: Demand Analysis
rows.note: Demand the ASSET must serve - load, throughput, growth. Closed 2026-08-29 at 17.1. 3.1 continues to forecast WORK demand and crew capacity, which is a different thing with the same word; both now exist and are distinguishable.

rows.name: Sustainable Development
rows.note: Waste, salvage and hazardous materials closed 2026-08-29 at 19.3. Sustainability as an objective-setting subject remains out of scope: it belongs to the asset management system above this process reference.

rows.name: Planning
rows.note: Closed 2026-08-29. 17.2 determines the solution, 17.4 builds and monitors the capital programme. 12.5 continues to define maintenance strategy and 12.6.3 replacement and renewal.

rows.name: Decision-Making
rows.note: Prioritisation, approval routing and asset risk. The model expresses these as DMN decision tables, which is exactly the auditability GFMAM asks for.

rows.name: Life cycle Value Realization
rows.note: Closed 2026-08-29. 17.5 establishes the whole-life cost basis, compares intervention options over the life cycle and evaluates outcomes against the investment case. This is what ISO 55001:2024 cl. 8.1 requires and the model previously did not do.

rows.name: Resourcing Strategy and Management
rows.note: Forecast, roster, crew management, workforce administration, contractor qualification.

rows.name: Shutdown and Outage Strategy and Planning
rows.note: GFMAM defines this as "An organisation's processes for the identification, planning, scheduling, execution, and control of work related to shutdowns, turnarounds, or outages (STOs)." All five verbs are now present: 18.1 identification and planning, 18.2 scheduling, 18.4 execution, 18.4.4 and 18.5 control. This subject and APQC 14.1.6 together are why the Asset Lifecycle band exists.

rows.name: Contingency Planning & Resilience Analysis
rows.note: Major events, mutual aid and wildfire response are the response side. There is no resilience analysis ahead of the event.

rows.name: Asset Management Leadership
rows.note: Organisational subject.

rows.name: Organisational Arrangements
rows.note: Organisational subject.

rows.name: Organisational Culture
rows.note: Organisational subject.

rows.name: Competence Management
rows.note: Skills and certification, which the model correctly treats as gating work assignment rather than as an HR record.

rows.name: Organisational Change Management
rows.note: Organisational subject.

rows.name: Knowledge Management
rows.note: Job plan and task libraries, and the document set at the place of work.

rows.name: Asset Management Data & Information Strategy
rows.note: System of record by asset class, and data quality and master data.

rows.name: Asset Management Data & Information Systems
rows.note: Integration and data exchange, with the IEC 61968-6 component set as the landscape.

rows.name: Configuration Management
rows.note: Asset specifications and as-built update. No configuration baseline or version control over the asset configuration itself.

rows.name: Systems Engineering
rows.note: Engineering discipline rather than a work management process.

rows.name: Asset Creation & Acquisition
rows.note: Closed 2026-08-29. 19.1 commissions, coordinates energisation and hands the asset over into service, completing the chain that 2.1 designs and 4.2 builds. Land and property acquisition remains out of scope - corporate real estate, APQC 10.1.

rows.name: Integrated Reliability
rows.note: Performance and reliability analysis, and failure mode validation. No reliability engineering feedback loop into design.

rows.name: Asset Operation
rows.note: The work-facing half is closed at 18.0: planned switching, clearance, coordination and return to service. 9.0 covers unplanned operation. Real-time monitoring, alarm handling, optimisation and protection settings stay OUT OF SCOPE BY DECISION - they are SCADA, ADMS and DERMS functions.

rows.name: Maintenance Delivery
rows.note: The model's centre of gravity and its most complete subject. 7.0 vegetation was missing from this row until Grok pointed out that vegetation IS maintenance delivery - the crosswalk was thin, not the category.

rows.name: Asset Repurposing or Disposal
rows.note: Closed 2026-08-29. 19.2 decommissions physically, 19.3 handles waste and salvage, 19.4 transfers ownership and closes the record. 12.1.6 continues to retire the record and 5.3 the accounting.
